title: record:quick_actions — renderer reads `aria.label`, the one spelling the platform ARIA contract refuses; and the registration's `actionNames` description claims an empty-bar fallback the renderer does not implement
body:
Found while implementing objectstack-ai/objectstack#8744 (declaring `record:quick_actions`' `ComponentPropsMap` row from the renderer's measured read points at `665661ab0932`). Two producer-side defects in the same component, filed together; unassigned.

## 1. The `aria` read point uses a spelling the shared ARIA shape refuses

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-quick-actions.tsx` (toolbar element):

```
aria-label={schema.aria?.label || 'Quick actions'}
```

`@objectstack/spec`'s `AriaPropsSchema` — the platform-wide ARIA contract this bag is supposed to carry — declares `ariaLabel` and REFUSES `label` (it is that shape's alias entry, i.e. a rename prescription pointing at `ariaLabel`). So at this pin:

- the spec-valid spelling `aria: { ariaLabel: '…' }` reaches the renderer and is read by nothing (`aria?.label` is undefined → built-in "Quick actions" fallback);
- the spelling the renderer honours, `aria: { label: '…' }`, is exactly what the spec refuses.

Because of that, objectstack#8744 deliberately does NOT declare `aria` on the new `RecordQuickActionsProps` row — declaring `AriaPropsSchema` there would mint `ariaLabel` as a declared-but-unenforced key (the #8691 `icon` class). The row carries a `guidance` refusal naming this issue instead, and declares `aria` the day the renderer reads the contract spelling.

**Fix direction:** read `schema.aria?.ariaLabel` (keeping `?.label` as a back-compat read if stored documents carry it is objectui's call), then the spec row declares `aria: AriaPropsSchema` in a follow-up. Note `SchemaRenderer`'s generic channel (`resolveAriaProps`) reads FLAT `schema.ariaLabel` off the hoisted node and passes `aria-label` as a component prop — which this renderer also drops (`splitDesigner` spreads only the designer keys) — so the nested-bag read in the renderer is the one live path for an authored label here.

## 2. The registration's `actionNames` description claims a fallback that does not exist

`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`, `ComponentRegistry.register('quick_actions', …)`:

> 'Action names to expose, in order (else every action declared for the object at this location)'

Measured at the same pin: when `actionNames` is absent and the host passes no `actions`, `namesToResolve` is empty → `needsLookup` is false → no metadata lookup happens → `actions` is `[]` → the bar renders its dashed "no actions configured" placeholder. There is no "every action declared for the object" fallback on any path. The description feeds Studio tooling and misled objectstack#8744's dispatch prompt verbatim (its declared-inputs list is quoted there as a claim to verify — this is the clause that failed verification). Either implement the fallback or fix the sentence; objectstack#8744's row documents the measured behaviour either way.
